If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, reduce forecast by 1.5–2.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid overconfidence bias.  
If sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and price is trending upward, shift forecast downward by 0.8–1.2% for mid horizon (8–15 days) to counteract sentiment-driven overreaction.  
If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and forecast is above 80, apply a 2–3% downward correction for late horizon (16–30 days) to align with bearish sentiment momentum.  
When sentiment swings from positive to negative within 5 days, reduce forecast slope by 0.5–1.0% per day for early horizon to prevent momentum reversal misjudgment.  
If sentiment is positive but price is declining, apply a 1–1.5% upward correction to forecast for mid horizon to offset sentiment-driven optimism.  
If sentiment is negative and forecast is below 70, increase forecast by 0.5–1.0% for late horizon to avoid underestimating rebound potential.
